terms.comment: Classically a plunderer (Cic.), later a kidnapper, and in Martial a literary thief (Lewis & Short).
Effrāctārius, a housebreaker, is in Seneca (Lewis & Short).
Classically a plagiārius is an oppressor or a kidnapper (Lewis & Short), and in Martial a plagiarist; the burglar fits a hacker better.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
